items.title: Transparency on trial: Mapping courts’ compliance with the RTI Act
items.summary: The effectiveness of the Right to Information (RTI) regime has, in recent years, come under a cloud of uncertainty with commentators pointing at a progressive weakening of RTI mechanisms. Among the concerns are onerous delays in appointments of information commissioners and other officials, rising backlogs and arbitrary rejections of requests by public authorities . The amendment effected to Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act by the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023 further exacerbated these concerns as it empowered public authorities to deny information if it qualified as ‘personal information’, without requiring it to be weighed against public interest. While the High Courts and the Supreme Court often find themselves adjudicating upon the failure of government ministries and departments to comply with the RTI Act, the courts themselves are guilty of not adhering to the principles of the Act.
